## The common configuration I pursued

The retained topology has an external air–liquid contactor feeding a continuously operating hydrogen-evolving cathode. An AEM transfers captured carbon ions into a separate anolyte, where hydrogen oxidation releases CO₂. The resulting CO₂/H₂ stream passes through hydrogen recovery and product drying; hydrogen returns to the electrochemical circuit.

This removes the predecessor’s stored-electrode charge swing, 176 electrical sections and assumed electrode-liquid displacement response. It introduces explicit obligations: mixed-ion transport, dissolved oxygen, hydrogen loss, potassium crossover, water return, gas cleanup and any catalyst-reset operation.

The basic AEM/hydrogen carbonate-regeneration mechanism already exists experimentally. Its measured geometry tradeoff is directly relevant: removing a 1 mm cathode gap approximately halved resistance, but carbon Faradaic efficiency fell to about 35% above 20 mA/cm² because generated hydroxide crossed the membrane without transporting carbon. The smaller resistance and the better carbon efficiency belong to different configurations. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

### One membrane, with simultaneous properties

I constructed a reacting Nernst–Planck model that conserves **total carbon and equivalent charge**, while allowing carbonate, bicarbonate, hydroxide and neutral CO₂ to interconvert inside the membrane. It includes the membrane potential consistently with the hydrogen electrodes.

One illustrative, explicitly unmeasured material tuple gives:

| Property or operating condition | Value |
|---|---:|
| Fixed positive charge | 1.5 mol/L of membrane phase |
| Membrane thickness | 50 µm |
| Bicarbonate, carbonate and neutral-CO₂ diffusivity | Each \(10^{-10}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}\) |
| Hydroxide diffusivity | \(3\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}\) |
| CO₂ boundary pressures | 336 ppm / 0.88 bar |
| Active fraction of physical main membrane | 90% |
| Carbon-equivalent current over physical main area | 10 mA/cm² |

**That same configuration** produces:

| Calculated response | Result |
|---|---:|
| Membrane resistance | 0.617 Ω·cm² |
| Charge per net carbon | 3.045 electrons/CO₂ |
| Electrical current on active area | 33.84 mA/cm² |
| Membrane work | 52.39 kJ/mol |
| Cell work after an assumed additional 1 Ω·cm² and 50 mV electrode-pair loss | **77.03 kJ/mol** |
